title: About
body:

简体中文

Hi! My name is Zhen Dong (Tangliengim: 진ˎ덩ꞈ, Romanised: Jìn-tông), and welcome to TheHokkienLang.

This site documents my work on Tangliengim (東寧音당ˉ롕임ˆ), a sound-based writing system for Hokkien built on the foundation of Hangul. Hokkien has always been a spoken language first, and writing it naturally has never been simple. Chinese characters and Romanisation systems are useful, but they do not always show how Hokkien sounds, especially its tones and tone sandhi — or what I would call “the essence of Hokkien”.

So why is it called Tangliengim? This project began during my time studying in Tainan, the city where Koxinga’s (鄭成功) Kingdom of Tungning (東寧國) was based. As a speaker of Singaporean Hokkien, I was also able to connect with Taiwanese Hokkien speakers there through the language we shared. Places such as Dongning Road (東寧路) and NCKU’s Dong-Ning Campus (成功大學東寧校區) became familiar to me. So the name Tangliengim (東寧音) carries both personal and historical meaning.

Whether you are a serious learner or just casually exploring, feel free to look around, read the stories, and see how Hokkien can be written in a new way.
